direction_notes: TUS to dmPFC, hippocampus, and anterior/dorsomedial thalamus each significantly reduced the influence of the model-derived reversal estimate on choice switching relative to sham, but in different ways: dmPFC TUS abolished the influence of nearly all decision variables (reversal estimate, uncertainty) leaving only recent reward history; hippocampus TUS selectively removed the influence of the reversal estimate; thalamus TUS reversed the sign of the reversal estimate's influence on switching.

timing.protocol_description: TUS was delivered bilaterally (40 s to the left hemisphere, 40 s to the right hemisphere) using a duty cycle of 30%, pulse length of 30 ms, and pulse repetition interval of 100 ms. This was an offline protocol: monkeys began the behavioural task 5-10 minutes after stimulation ended. Each stimulation condition (dmPFC, hippocampus, thalamus, or sham) was repeated 5-8 times per animal on separate days, at least 24 hours apart, with a sham day scheduled at the start and end of the series.

source_quotes.n_subjects: To test this possibility, in experiment 2, we trained three new macaques to perform the correlated task and examined the impact of disrupting activity in dmPFC, hippocampus, and anterior and dorsomedial thalamus with transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS).

flags.reason: Paper states 'each stimulation condition was repeated 5-8 times for each animal' (per target/sham condition, not a single total-sessions count); recorded as the stated range.
Paper describes the order of TUS targets as 'pseudo-randomized' rather than fully randomised; recorded as true.
Sham TUS matched the real procedure except that 'sonication was not triggered although the TUS sound was simulated'; classified as sound_only_sham.
Paper refers to the thalamic target variably as 'anterior medial thalamus' and 'anterior and dorsomedial thalamus'; both anterior_thalamic_nucleus and mediodorsal_nucleus terms are given.
TUS effects differed qualitatively across the three targets (loss of influence vs. reversal of influence direction), so classified as mixed_or_unclear.
